value.text: Dì di santa Maria della neve / addj 5 daghossto 1473

claims.statement: Inscription at upper left, written right to left in mirror script: 'Dì di s[an]ta Maria della neve / addj 5 daghossto 1473' ('The day of Santa Maria della Neve, on the 5th of August 1473'). The translation is the compiler's.

sources.cite: Lombardia Beni Culturali, photographic record of the drawing, transcription of the inscription. Read through search engine excerpts in this session; the page itself was not fetched in this session.

claims.statement: The date 5 August 1473 is written on the sheet; this dates the inscription, and by usual inference the drawing.

claims.statement: A second note on the verso, written left to right, is reported as 'Io Morando d'Antoni[o] sono chontento' ('I, Morando d'Antonio, am content'). Its hand and meaning are not established here.

sources.cite: arte.it, Leonardo, Paesaggio, catalogue page. Read through search engine excerpts in this session; the page itself was not fetched in this session.

value.text: Valdinievole and Padule di Fucecchio seen from Montalbano

claims.statement: The view is identified as the Valdinievole and the Padule di Fucecchio seen from Montalbano; other texts say only that it is a landscape in the Arno valley, probably near Vinci. The identification of the view is an interpretation.

sources.cite: Museo Galileo, itinerary 'Youthful period in Florence'. Read through search engine excerpts in this session; the page itself was not fetched in this session.

value.text: Inscription and verso note in different directions

claims.statement: Press reports of 2019 Uffizi studies took the two directions of writing (mirror script on the recto, conventional on the verso) as evidence that Leonardo wrote with both hands. This is a reading, not a statement on the sheet.

sources.cite: Artnet News, report on 2019 study of the 1473 landscape. Read through search engine excerpts in this session; the page itself was not fetched in this session.

open_questions: Does the verso note 'Io Morando d'Antonio sono chontento' belong to Leonardo's hand, and what does it record?
